title: When the Salt Falls
premise: In the salt-locked valley of Veyra, magic cannot cross the white flats, and the last guild of the Unmarked has hidden there for generations. When the crown declares a kingdom-wide hunt for the gifted, Zephyrine Vasquez — youngest of a dying guild, secretly carrying his grandmother's unregistered gift — is dragged beyond the valley as bait in a plot he barely understands. He discovers the king himself is bound to an ancient entity wearing the crown like a parasite, sustained by harvested gifts, and that Zephyrine's own bloodline holds the binding's original knot. To free the king he must surrender the inheritance that makes him belong to his guild, choose between the valley that raised him and the hunted girl who taught him the outside world, and finally unmake the crown at the cost of the gift itself.
about_author: Xanthe Ishikawa is a former cartographer who spent six years mapping coastal salt flats before turning to fiction full-time. She writes fantasy about borders — geographic, magical, and emotional — from a small house that floods every spring.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. On the eve of the guild's Founding Rite, Zephyrine hides the flicker of inherited magic that surfaces whenever he touches salt-crusted stone. His grandmother warns him the valley's protection is thinning. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath ritual comfort; belonging shown as something already cracking.

chapters.title: A Summons in White
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. A royal courier crosses the flats — impossible, since no rider survives them — bearing a decree: all gifted persons must present themselves for 'census.' The guild elder votes to send their youngest as a decoy. Emotional beat: betrayal by the people who raised him, masked as duty.

chapters.title: Crossing the Flats
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Guided by the courier Sereth, Zephyrine steps past the valley's boundary and feels his gift roar awake for the first time — overwhelming, terrifying, alive. He collapses at the far shore. Emotional beat: awe and grief; leaving home means becoming someone new.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Hunts Hunters
chapters.summary: Maren's POV introduced. Maren, a fugitive gift-thief turned rescuer, ambushes the courier party and frees Zephyrine, believing him a captive. He lies about being gifted. Emotional beat: wary alliance; first spark of trust built on mutual deception.

chapters.title: Road of Ash Bells
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Traveling through burned villages where gifted children were taken, Maren teaches Zephyrine to shield his power while he secretly heals a dying farmer's blight. Emotional beat: guilt deepening into resolve; the hunt becomes personal.

chapters.title: The Census House
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. They infiltrate a census house where confiscated gifts are stored in glass reliquaries. Zephyrine recognizes his grandmother's handwriting on one label. Emotional beat: horror and recognition; the crown isn't cataloguing gifts, it's harvesting them.

chapters.title: What Wears the Crown
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. In the capital, they witness the king at a public rite — and Zephyrine alone sees the thing coiled beneath the crown, feeding on the reliquaries. It looks back at him. Emotional beat: cold terror; being seen by something ancient.

chapters.title: An Inheritance of Knots
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Decoding his grandmother's letters, Zephyrine learns the Vasquez line wove the original binding that caged the entity inside the crown — and that the valley exists to hide the final knot: him. Emotional beat: shattering revelation; he was never hidden, he was kept.

chapters.title: The Court of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Posing as a census clerk, Zephyrine gains palace access and meets the king privately. The king, lucid for one breathless hour, begs for release and names the price: the binder's own gift, freely given. Emotional beat: compassion for the enemy; duty and mercy entangling.

chapters.title: Sereth's Bargain
chapters.summary: Sereth's POV. The courier, revealed as the entity's agent, offers Zephyrine immunity for his guild if he surrenders willingly. Zephyrine stalls, learning the entity plans to consume the valley next. Emotional beat: temptation and clarity; safety offered at the cost of everything he loves.

chapters.title: Salt on Her Hands
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren discovers Zephyrine's deception about his gift and his bloodline. Their fight in a rain-soaked alley turns into confession — her stolen gift, his inherited one, both orphans of other people's choices. Emotional beat: rupture into intimacy; love admitted mid-anger.

chapters.title: The Guild Answers
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Survivors of his guild arrive in the capital, led by his grandmother, who reveals she sent him out deliberately: only a Vasquez raised outside fear can face the crown. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed as faith; belonging redefined rather than restored.

chapters.title: Night of Glass Bells
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The entity, aware of the plan, purges the reliquary vaults to grow strong. The guild's desperate raid saves three hundred bottled gifts but costs the elder her life. Emotional beat: costly victory; grief sharpening purpose into a deadline.

chapters.title: The Binding Rite, Undone
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Studying the original knot, Zephyrine realizes unbinding requires not destroying the entity but releasing it — and it will take the nearest vessel: the king, or him. Emotional beat: dread of choice; heroism as arithmetic of sacrifice.

chapters.title: Coronation of Ash
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The entity accelerates its timetable, forcing a false coronation of the king's heir as a new host. The city seals its gates. Maren and Sereth clash openly; Sereth hesitates for the first time. Emotional beat: rising panic; even servants of the thing can flinch.

chapters.title: What the Valley Kept
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. His grandmother performs the last preparation: returning to Zephyrine the fragment of gift she hid in the valley's salt, making him whole — and fully visible to the entity. Emotional beat: completion and exposure; strength arriving inseparable from danger.

chapters.title: The Long Walk Up
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The companions fight through the sealed palace to the throne room as the entity begins consuming the heir. Sereth turns against it, buying the doorway with her life. Emotional beat: momentum of sacrifice; every ally pays a toll.

chapters.title: Crown of Teeth
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Climax. Before the entity, Zephyrine offers his whole gift freely — the one condition it cannot refuse — and begins the unbinding as the king's mind briefly resurfaces to hold the knot open. Emotional beat: transcendence through surrender; love for strangers as the weapon.

chapters.title: Unbound
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The entity tears free and dissolves into the sea wind; the king dies human and grateful, the crown crumbling to rust. Zephyrine survives but hollowed, his gift gone. Emotional beat: exhausted aftermath; victory that feels like amputation.

chapters.title: The Empty Gift
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Recovering in the palace infirmary, Zephyrine grieves the loss of the inheritance that defined him, while freed gifts return to their scattered owners across the kingdom. Emotional beat: identity rebuilt without magic; mourning as proof of love.

chapters.title: Homecoming, Rewritten
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Zephyrine and Maren cross the flats together — the valley now lets the gifted pass both ways. The guild, no longer dying but changed, votes to become a school rather than a refuge. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not inherited; home expanded.

chapters.title: When the Salt Falls
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Epilogue. A year later, at the Founding Rite, Zephyrine teaches unmarked children alongside gifted ones, and salt falls like snow over the valley — ordinary weather now, not a wall. He keeps his grandmother's empty reliquary on the sill. Emotional beat: peace earned; inheritance transformed into legacy.
